review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of the two normalizer lemmas. Only the in-file uses matter here, because the other matches are different declarations in other namespaces. I looked for repeated reasoning across centerOf_map, normalizer_map_inf_range, mem_normalizer_map_iff, SiegelRadicalData.map and SiegelModuleData.of_model. I found three repeated blocks. Lean was not run, so the proposed rewrites are untested. The centralizer_le proof is a single long argument with no repeated part. The name `normalizer_map_inf_range_le_of_mem` below is a proposed new name.

findings.problem: The `h1` argument is written out twice: `comap_normalizer_eq_of_le_range`, then `rw [comap_map_eq_self_of_injective hι] at h1`. It proves that the comap of the normalizer of the image is the normalizer of the original subgroup. `normalizer_map_inf_range` (lines 33–36) does this inline and then manually transports membership with `h1 ▸ (hy : ...)`. `mem_normalizer_map_iff` (lines 44–47) proves exactly the pointwise statement that this step needs, but it is declared after its only natural client and is not used by it.
findings.proposed_change: Put `mem_normalizer_map_iff` first and keep its proof. Then shorten the forward direction of `normalizer_map_inf_range` to `rintro _ ⟨hy, x, rfl⟩; exact Subgroup.mem_map.mpr ⟨x, (mem_normalizer_map_iff hι U x).mp hy, rfl⟩`. The hypotheses are the same, namely `hι : Function.Injective ι` and `U : Subgroup P`. The reverse direction (line 39) is unchanged.
findings.benefit: The comap/normalizer argument then appears once. A reader sees that the `⊓ ι.range` lemma is a corollary of the pointwise iff, and the awkward `▸` cast on line 37 goes away.

have hx1 : ι x ∈ (Subgroup.normalizer (U : Set P)).map ι := ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
      rw [← normalizer_map_inf_range hι] at hx1
findings.problem: Two proofs repeat the same step. Given `x ∈ normalizer U`, they use `normalizer_map_inf_range` to show `ι x ∈ normalizer (U.map ι) ⊓ ι.range`. Then they apply a hypothesis that is stated for that subgroup. In `coatom` this is `hM` (lines 74–78). In `of_model.irred` it is `hN` (lines 113–116, the `hx1` lines are 114–115). The resulting statement is exactly what is needed, but it is rebuilt by hand each time.
findings.proposed_change: Add a small lemma after `normalizer_map_inf_range`: `theorem map_mem_normalizer_inf_range {ι : P →* Y} (hι : Function.Injective ι) {U : Subgroup P} {x : P} (hx : x ∈ Subgroup.normalizer (U : Set P)) : ι x ∈ Subgroup.normalizer ((U.map ι : Subgroup Y) : Set Y) ⊓ ι.range`. Its proof is `(normalizer_map_inf_range hι U) ▸ ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩`, or `⟨(mem_normalizer_map_iff hι U x).mpr hx, x, rfl⟩`. Then `hN` becomes `fun x hx => hM (map_mem_normalizer_inf_range hι hx)`. In `of_model`, replace lines 114–116 by `have h2 := hN (map_mem_normalizer_inf_range hι hx)`.
findings.benefit: The transport of the normalizer into `normalizer ⊓ range` gets one name and one proof. The two Siegel-data proofs then read as direct applications of the hypothesis.

findings.problem: The same element-chasing proof appears twice, at lines 64–67 (`B ≤ T.map ι` gives `B.comap ι ≤ T`) and at lines 107–110 (`W ≤ U.map ι` gives `W.comap ι ≤ U`). Both unpack `mem_map`, then use injectivity to get `x = t`. This is the standard fact that `comap_map_eq_self_of_injective` gives `(T.map ι).comap ι = T`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma, e.g. `theorem comap_le_of_le_map {ι : P →* Y} (hι : Function.Injective ι) {B : Subgroup Y} {T : Subgroup P} (h : B ≤ T.map ι) : B.comap ι ≤ T := (Subgroup.comap_mono h).trans (Subgroup.comap_map_eq_self_of_injective hι T).le`. Then use `comap_le_of_le_map hι hBT` at line 64 and `comap_le_of_le_map hι hWU` at line 107. This works under each site's hypotheses, since `hBT : B ≤ T.map ι` and `hWU : W ≤ U.map ι` are both in scope. It may also be worth checking whether Mathlib already has this under a different name.
findings.benefit: Each 4-line element chase becomes a one-line call. The injectivity argument sits in one place, next to the other `map`/`comap` transport lemmas in the file.
